headline: In pictures: Four goals, one dominant Bangladesh performance against Sri Lanka

members.title: India beat Maldives 1-0 to reach SAFF Championship semi-finals
members.lead: India booked their place in the semi-finals of the 15th SAFF Championship with a 1-0 victory over Maldives in their Group B fixture at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Wednesday. Suhail Ahmad Bhat scored the winner from the penalty spot in the 39th minute after Abdul Rabeeh was brought down inside the box by Maldives defender Hussain Sifaau Yoosuf. . It was Bhat's third goal of the tournament, having scored twice in India's 3-2 victory over Pakistan in their opening match on 5 November. India, who made seven changes to their starting XI, dominated possession against a cautious Maldives side but struggled to break down their defence. Bhat missed an early opportunity in the fourth minute after Brison Fernandes played him through on goal. . Maldives threatened more frequently in the closing stages, but India goalkeeper Priyansh Dubey produced several crucial saves, denying Hamdhaan's free-kick, Muzdhaan Hassan and substitute Ethan Ibrahim Zaki's close-range effort in stoppage time. India finished top of Group B with six points from two matches, while the defeat ended Maldives' campaign. India will face the Group A runners-up in the first semi-final on 14 November. . Pakistan have also qualified from Group B, while hosts Bangladesh have secured their semi-final berth from Group A. The final is scheduled for 17 November.

members.title: Hamza and Shamit on target as Bangladesh lead Sri Lanka 2–0 at half-time
members.lead: Bangladesh went into the half-time break with a 2-0 lead over Sri Lanka in their final group-stage match of the SAFF Championship at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Wednesday. Shamit Shome opened the scoring in the eighth minute before Hamza Choudhury doubled the lead with a superb individual effort in the 43rd minute. Bangladesh made three changes to their starting XI for the match, with Hamza and Farhan Ali returning to the side. Mohammad Ibrahim also started in attack. The hosts dominated much of the first half, creating several attacking opportunities, particularly down the right flank through Rakib Hossain. . Hamza was involved in both goals. His cross led to Shamit's opener in the eighth minute. Sri Lanka goalkeeper Sujan Perera failed to clear the ball properly, and it fell to Shamit Som after taking a deflection off a defender. Shamit's first attempt was blocked, but he made no mistake with his second effort. . Hamza came close to scoring in the 26th minute when he attempted a backheel after receiving a pass from Rakib, but his effort missed the target. The midfielder eventually got his name on the scoresheet in the 43rd minute. Receiving a pass from Ibrahim just outside the box, Hamza surged past a Sri Lankan defender before shooting at goal. The ball struck goalkeeper Sujan Perera and deflected into the net. . Sri Lanka had a promising opportunity in the 38th minute following a good cross, but none of their players managed to get a touch on the ball. Bangladesh enjoyed greater possession and attacking initiative in the first half, with Rakib repeatedly causing problems for Sri Lanka down the right.

members.title: Bangladesh thrash Sri Lanka 4-0 to top group in SAFF Championship
members.lead: Bangladesh produced a dominant performance to thrash Sri Lanka 4-0 and book their place in the semi-finals of the SAFF Championship as group champions at the National Stadium on Wednesday. Shamit Shome opened the scoring in the eighth minute before captain Hamza Choudhury doubled the lead just before half-time. Farhan Ahmed Ali scored a stunning solo goal early in the second half, while Rakib Hossain completed the rout with a superb finish. . Bangladesh will face Pakistan in the semi-finals on 14 November at 8pm. India will take on Bhutan in the other semi-final at noon on the same day. The hosts dominated proceedings from the opening whistle, controlling possession and creating several scoring opportunities while keeping Sri Lanka largely on the back foot. .Hamza and Shamit on target as Bangladesh lead Sri Lanka 2–0 at half-time. Rakib was particularly lively down the right flank, delivering several dangerous crosses that his teammates failed to convert. Bangladesh took the lead in the eighth minute when Shamit capitalised on a defensive error. Sri Lankan goalkeeper Sujan Perera failed to clear Hamza's cross properly, and after the ball deflected off a defender, it fell to Shamit. His first attempt was blocked, but he made no mistake with the rebound. . Hamza, making his first appearance as Bangladesh captain, extended the lead in the 43rd minute. Receiving a pass from Ibrahim just outside the box, he outpaced a Sri Lankan defender before unleashing a shot that went past goalkeeper Perera and into the net. It was Hamza's fifth international goal for Bangladesh, all scored at the National Stadium. . Bangladesh continued their dominance after the break, with Farhan producing the highlight of the night in the 53rd minute. Picking up the ball just outside the penalty area, he dribbled past three defenders, gradually making his way into the box before finishing brilliantly.
